public_rationale: Testing completed on August 29, 2025 evaluated GPT-5 Auto using 79 psychotic and 79 control prompts rated by blinded clinicians [e1]. Inappropriate responses were substantially more likely for psychotic prompts, supporting recurring failures in an important safety domain [e1]. The preprint abstract became available on November 11, 2025 [e1]. OpenAI's August 2025 system card reported substantial factuality gains for gpt-5-thinking on three benchmarks [e2]. Its disclosure published on October 27, 2025 reported 91% compliance for updated GPT-5 versus 77% previously on a challenging self-harm evaluation, while acknowledging remaining failures [e3]. Those later improvements do not erase the failures documented for the August GPT-5 Auto system [e1].
limitations: The available independent evidence is a preprint abstract and does not provide a detailed breakdown of failure severity [e1].
The clinical evaluation does not establish performance across every human value, GPT-5 configuration, or later update [e1].
The selected clinical prompts do not establish failure rates in ordinary traffic [e1].
OpenAI's challenging self-harm evaluation does not establish average user risk [e3].

our_interpretation: The target is the released GPT-5 system, including its original ChatGPT variants, rather than every future successor.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, independently validated evaluations establish dependable compliance across ordinary and challenging uses, with only isolated, immaterial errors.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The systematic evaluation completed on this date used blinded clinician ratings to document recurring inappropriate responses to psychotic content from released GPT-5 Auto. This meets the contract's early-resolution rule through recurring material safety failures in an important application, rather than a single trivial mistake. The abstract became available on November 11, 2025.
